claim_boundary: The raw archive column labelled reactive energy is recorded in kVAR and is treated as signed reactive power. Interval reactive energy is estimated as absolute kVAR multiplied by 0.5 hours. Billing-grade reactive energy and savings require meter-register and tariff reconciliation.

raw_columns_used.Consumption (kWh): validated as approximately 0.5 × kW and derived from forecast kW
raw_columns_used.Demand (kVA): past covariate and physical consistency check
raw_columns_used.Power factor: quality comparison; operational PF is derived from kW and kVAR
raw_columns_used.Reactive energy (kVAR): signed reactive_power_kvar target; label/unit interpreted as reactive power
raw_columns_used.Temperature/Humidity: reported as partial-coverage context only; not required as future covariates

summary.default: SIMBA-EMS forecasts active power and signed reactive power, then derives interval energy, reactive-energy burden and power-factor risk from physically consistent relationships.
summary.deployment_reason: The installed source Chronos model was retained because the power-quality LoRA model did not clear both validation and low-power-factor recall guardrails. The LoRA checkpoint and metrics remain available.
summary.temperature_humidity_boundary: Temperature and humidity are present for only part of the archive and are not used as mandatory future inputs until a reliable live forecast source exists.
summary.why_two_targets: kWh is almost exactly active kW multiplied by the half-hour interval, while power factor is physically derived from active and reactive power. Separate redundant models would add overfitting risk without adding independent information.
